Tool approval rule

Installation default for future tool invocations. Tool grants, deny rules, and required high-risk approvals remain authoritative.

Deployment: Local development

Approval rule

Ask for risky work
Skip normal prompts

Low risk allowed tools can run, but Medium, High, and Critical risk work asks first. Connectors set to let reads or changes run on their own are the exception.

Apply my Settings and Capabilities changes without asking first

Off by default. When on, Settings changes such as the network allowlist, connectors and skills you install from Capabilities, and skills you switch on there apply right away instead of waiting for your approval.

Refresh

Current: Off

Apply my Settings and Capabilities changes without asking first
Covers saves through the Settings forms, such as the network allowlist, Firecrawl, approval mode and runtime switches, connectors you install from Capabilities, and skills you switch on from Capabilities. A skill you install from Capabilities installs and switches on without asking; when this is off, each of those two steps asks. GoatCitadel sign-in, API keys and other credentials still ask for approval.
Turning a skill off, or pausing one that is on, from Capabilities applies right away even when this is off, because it only takes power away; a remote-hardened install still asks. Skill changes made anywhere else, such as Chat's skill commands, still ask.
Change requests a model makes in Chat still need your approval. Anything that can call the Settings or Capabilities API as you, such as a script on this computer while GoatCitadel sign-in is off, can also make these changes without one.
Each Settings change and connector install is still recorded as a change plan, with its audit trail and any undo it supports. A skill switch, and each step of a skill install, keeps its approval, marked as approved by you, with the reason.
Turning this on needs one last approval. A remote-hardened install ignores it.
Save setting
Browser errands

Browser errands let GoatCitadel use its own Chrome window on this PC, with your saved logins, to do tasks you ask for. It asks before spending money, sending, deleting, or changing account settings, and hands sign-ins to you. Reading and browsing don't ask, so a hostile page could try to steer it into carrying your information to another site. Sites may notice an automated browser and limit your account.

Refresh

Current: Off

Let Chat do errands in its own browser window

Errands also need Web access turned on in Chat. While Web access is Off, Chat does not offer browser errands.

Save setting
Where errand approvals go
None

When you're away from the PC, errand approvals go here and to your phone if you haven't answered in 30 seconds. Until the phone app update ships, your phone can see and deny them; approve them in the window, in Chat, or in a channel.

No private conversation of yours is listed yet. Message GoatCitadel from your own account on a channel, then choose “This is you” for that account in the channel’s people list.

Filesystem write roots

Folders outside the workspace where Chat's filesystem tools may write, such as a temp folder to clean. Deny-wins and approvals
